articleTitle: A Non-Local Means Denoising Co-Processor with Data Reuse Scheme and Dual-Clock Domain for High Resolution Image Sensor
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Integrated Circuits, Technologies and Applications (ICTA)
abstract: This paper presents a non-local means (NLM) co-processor with data reuse scheme and dual-clock domain for high resolution image sensor The key features are as follows: 1) The NLM is accelerated by the parallel pixel-level pipeline architecture with a compact single-port SRAM-based line buffer for serial-parallel conversion. 2) The algorithm is optimized by using L1 loss calculation instead of the L2 loss calculation for Similarity computing, and the fitted quantized look-up-table for exponential operations to reduce logic utilization; 3) the data reuse method for the weights calculation reduces the area of the corresponding circuit by 6/7; 4) Most of the parallel computing are implemented in the fast core, which runs at twice the pixel clock frequency, thus halve the amount of computation per cycle. The architecture achieves a real-time denoising at 60 frames/second for full high definition (FHD <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbf{1920}\times \mathbf{1080}$</tex>) videos with the energy efficiency of only 36.22 mW/frame.

articleTitle: A High-Throughput and Configurable TRNG Based on Dual-Mode Memristor for Stochastic Computing
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Integrated Circuits, Technologies and Applications (ICTA)
abstract: In this work, a novel configurable true random number generator (TRNG) based on VO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>/HfO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> stacked dual-mode memristor is demonstrated. The <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbf{V}_{\mathbf{th}}$</tex> fluctuation in the volatile IMT mode of the device is exploited as the entropy source for the TRNG, ensuring the generation of high-quality random numbers. Additionally, the non-volatile RRAM mode allows for in situ control of the TRNG's on/off state. The proposed TRNG achieves a high throughput of 5 Mb/s, enabling seamless integration into a stochastic computing (SC) system for image edge detection. The experimental result showcases superior performance with an average error rate as low as 0.73% with a bitstream length of 256.

articleTitle: Towards Energy-Efficient Asynchronous Circuit Design with Flip-Flop-to-Latch Replacement
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Integrated Circuits, Technologies and Applications (ICTA)
abstract: With data flow controlled by handshake templates, asynchronous circuits have the potential for low power consumption and high performance. However, the control of the handshake signal introduces additional hardware overhead. We utilize latch to further reduce the power consumption, then propose an efficient design methodology for a latch-based asynchronous pipeline and timing constraints method with conventional EDA tools. An asynchronous RISC-V processor was designed and thoroughly compared with its synchronous counterpart and the popular RISC-V cores to validate the effectiveness of the proposed methodology. Experimental results demonstrate a 3.5% area optimization and a 14.9% reduction in power consumption compared with the synchronous counterpart.

articleTitle: A Monolithic Integrated E-Mode GaN 48V-to-1V DC-DC Buck Converter with PWM Control
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Integrated Circuits, Technologies and Applications (ICTA)
abstract: In this paper, a fully-integrated gallium-nitride (GaN) half-bridge DC-DC buck converter is designed based on GaN-on-SOI (silicon-on-insulator) technology. A self-bootstrap gate drive circuit is designed to achieve rail-to-rail gate driving while reducing the conduction loss of the switch. A level shifter is designed to transfer the gate drive control voltage from the low voltage (LV) region to the high voltage (HV) region. In addition, we design a fully-integrated closed-loop pulse-width modulation (PWM) control module for the buck converter. We have simulated the direct 48V-to-1V DC-DC with a maximum load current of 5A. At 250kHz, the half bridge DC-DC buck converter can achieve a peak efficiency of 84.3% at a load current of 3A.

articleTitle: A High-PSR High-Precision Fast-Transient-Response Capacitor-Free LDO for LiDAR Receiver SoC
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Integrated Circuits, Technologies and Applications (ICTA)
abstract: A capacitor-free low-dropout regulator (LDO) with high power-supply ripple rejection (PSR), high precision and fast transient response for LiDAR receiver SoC is presented. A ripple feedforward circuit (RFFC) and a ripple amplification circuit (RAC) are proposed to enhance the intermediate-frequency and high-frequency PSR respectively. Two additional loops have been put forward to improve both the accuracy and transient response of the conventional three-loop flipped-voltage-follower (FVF) structure. The proposed LDO has been designed in a 180-nm CMOS technology and simulated in Spectre. It can work under 2.2~3.4 V supply voltage range and the output voltage is 1.8 V, while the simulated zero-loading quiescent current is 220 µA to 308 µA under the whole supply range. With 260-pF output capacitance and maximum loading current of 100 mA, the low-frequency PSR of the proposed LDO can reach -75 dB, and the worst PSR is -7dB from DC to very high frequency as more than 1 GHz. The simulated voltage spike is less than 196 mV when the loading current changes between 0 and 100 mA with 100-ns edge time. The proposed LDO achieves competitive FoM<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1</inf> of 31.731 E+9 and FoM<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> of 1.57 ps.

articleTitle: A 400-Gb/s 64-QAM Optical Receiver with Monolithically Integrated TIA and Balanced-PD in 45-nm SOI CMOS
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Integrated Circuits, Technologies and Applications (ICTA)
abstract: This paper presents an analog coherent receiver front-end for high-speed optical links. By monolithically integrating two silicon photonic (Si-Ph) photodetectors (PD) with a differential-input transimpedance amplifier (TIA), a balanced topology and high receiving common-mode rejection ratio (CMRR) is realized. An inverter-based linear TIA with shunt-series multiple peaking is proposed to enable the high-order quadrature amplitude modulation (QAM). Simulation results show the TIA achieves 41 GHz bandwidth, 12.3 <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbf{pA}/\surd$</tex> Hz input referred noise. Implemented in a 45 nm Si-Ph CMOS process, the optical receiver reaches 400-Gb/s channel speed with 64-QAM modulation, at the cost of only 1.8495mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> chip area and 18.3 mW power consumption.

articleTitle: A High Voltage Bootstrapped Switch Based SAR ADC for Battery Management System
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Integrated Circuits, Technologies and Applications (ICTA)
abstract: This paper presents a novel high voltage bootstrapped switch (HVBS) that can sample a 4.5V input signal using a triple-well 65nm CMOS process without any drain-extended NMOS. Based on this HVBS, we designed a 12-bit Successive-Approximation-Register (SAR) analog-to-digital conversion (ADC) with configurable input range that can convert input signals with a range of 1.2V and 4.5V. This ADC achieves a Signal-to-Noise-and-Distortion Ratio (SNDR) of 65.2dB with an input range of 4.5V operating at 500kS/s and 1.2V supply, making it suitable for battery management systems (BMS).

articleTitle: A Power-Efficient $\boldsymbol{4}-\mathbf{V}_{\mathbf{ppd}}$ 128-Gb/s PAM-4 Optical Modulator Driver with Merged BV Doubler Topology in 130-nm BiCMOS
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Integrated Circuits, Technologies and Applications (ICTA)
abstract: This paper presents a power-efficient optical modulator driver circuit designed in 130-nm BiCMOS technology. The proposed driver circuit, based on the breakdown voltage (BV) doubler topology, achieves a significant reduction in power consumption and chip area by merging the data-path emitter-follower (EF) stage and the bias common-emitter (CE) stage into one single stage. The effectiveness of the proposed driver is confirmed by theoretical analysis and simulations. Compared with conventional BV doubler-based topology, the proposed driver improves the power consumption by 21% from 1.11W to 0.92W, with a -3-dB bandwidth of 49.0 GHz and an output voltage swing of 4 <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbf{V}_{\mathbf{ppd}}$</tex>. Simulation results also demonstrate that the proposed driver is capable of supporting PAM-4 optical communications at a data rate of 128 Gb/s, with an output PAM-4 eye width of 0.61 UI and a ratio of level mismatch (RLM) of 95%.

articleTitle: A Bio-Impedance Measurement Chip Design with AC Current Outputs
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Integrated Circuits, Technologies and Applications (ICTA)
abstract: This paper presents a bioimpedance measurement integrated circuit design and provides the chip test results and data analysis. The chip includes a voltage-based digital-to-analog converter (DAC) circuit, a low-pass filter (LPF) module, a selection circuit, and switches for logic control. The chip can output two AC currents, which input into the bio-impedance for measurement. The chip is designed and fabricated using SMIC 180-nm CMOS process. Measurement results show that a measurement range of 10K-1M Ω and a resolution of 15.2 m Ω / √Hz are achieved.

articleTitle: A 405ps/20% Delay Range, 7.4mW/ns BPF-Based Delay Cell with ISI Mitigation for 7.5-8.5GHz IR-UWB Beamforming Receivers
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Integrated Circuits, Technologies and Applications (ICTA)
abstract: This paper presents a BPF-based time delay cell for UWB phased array to suppress ISI in analog beamforming with low cost. Combined with phase shifter, the delay cell shows similar ISI mitigation performance to true-time-delay but consumes much lower power and area. A prototype 7.5-8.5GHz UWB receiver front end is implemented in 65nm CMOS. The proposed delay cell achieves a large delay range of 405ps and consumes 3.0mW.

articleTitle: NORP: A Compact Neuromorphic Olfactory Recognition Processor With On-Chip Hybrid Learning
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Integrated Circuits, Technologies and Applications (ICTA)
abstract: This work proposes a low-cost neuromorphic olfactory recognition processor for electronic noses. The processor targets a two-layer spiking neural network, enabling on-chip unsupervised spike-timing dependent plasticity (STDP) learning for the feature extraction layer and supervised spike-error dependent plasticity (SEDP) learning for the feature classification layer. An FPGA prototype of the SNN processor was implemented. It attained a comparably high accuracy of 96.25% at a 188 sample/s inference speed on the Twin Gas Sensor Arrays odor dataset.

articleTitle: A Reconfigurable High-Precision and Energy-Efficient Circuit Design of Sigmoid, Tanh and Softmax Activation Functions
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Integrated Circuits, Technologies and Applications (ICTA)
abstract: This paper proposes a reconfigurable circuit design for Sigmoid, Tanh and Softmax nonlinear functions using Coordinate Rotation Digital Computer (CORDIC) algorithm for deep neural network hardware accelerators. By exploiting arithmetic operation similarity, the proposed reconfigurable design reuses CORDIC units to implement the exponent and division operations in the nonlinear functions, and also utilizes the successive approximation property of CORDIC to achieves adjustable accuracy. In addition, Fast-Convergence CORDIC algorithm is employed to reduce the redundant iterations so as to effectively achieve high accuracy and low power consumption. FPGA implementation shows that it can achieve an adjustable precision range of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbf{1}\times \mathbf{10^{-1}}-\mathbf{3}\times \mathbf{10^{-3}}$</tex> with 948 LUTs and 189 FFs. At 100 MHz, it outperforms the conventional standalone designs, i.e., 42.6% and 26.5% increase in precision, 40.5%, 41.9% and 48.9% reduction in latency, and 21.5%, 18.5% and 9.6% increase in energy efficiency, respectively. The preliminary evaluation results in a case study shows that the accuracy loss of LSTM neural network using the proposed design is only 0.98% on Google Speech Command v2 keyword recognition task.

articleTitle: A W-Band Low-Noise Amplifier Using Gm-Boosting Technique with Weak Coupling
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Integrated Circuits, Technologies and Applications (ICTA)
abstract: This paper presents a W-band low-noise amplifier (LNA) using g<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">m</inf>-boosting technology with weak coupling. Utilizing the g<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">m</inf>-boosting technique to improve the gain and reduce post-stage noise. Neutralizing capacitors are used to reduce the effect of interconnect parasitics. Fabricated in a 65-nm SOI CMOS process, the proposed LNA achieves a peak gain of 16.2dB and a minimum noise figure of 7.8dB, while the -3dB bandwidth is 92 ~ 98GHz. It consumes 36mW with 1.2V and 1.8V supply and occupies 0.34 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>.

articleTitle: Temperature-Adaptive MRAM Sensing Using Varied Magneto-Resistance
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Integrated Circuits, Technologies and Applications (ICTA)
abstract: Magnetic tunnel junction (MTJ) shows temperature varied magneto-resistance characteristics. In this paper, we propose temperature adaptive reading circuits using MTJ as a sensor device with its self-reference and poly-resistor reference. Read margin can be effectively improved. Magnetic random-access memory (MRAM) array is implemented based on MTJ sensor and peripheral circuits. Simulation results show MRAM read and write performance over a wide temperature range of - 55°C-125°C.

articleTitle: ViT - and LSTM-Based FMCW Radar Target Recognition System
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Integrated Circuits, Technologies and Applications (ICTA)
abstract: With the development of deep learning technology, the applications of millimeter wave radar signal processing are increasing. This study proposes a radar target recognition (RTR) system for range-Doppler (RD) maps classification based on the visual transformer (ViT) model, which combines ViT and long short term memory (LSTM) architecture for the radar target recognition of human-vehicle classification scenario. The proposed architecture affords good accuracy and robustness as it simultaneously extracts the temporal and spatial information of an input image sequence. Moreover, this system achieves an accuracy rate of 99.6% in the classification of humans and vehicles, which is considerably higher than that obtained through traditional convolutional neural network (CNN) method.

articleTitle: An Energy-Efficient MAC Design with Error Compensation Using Hybrid Approximate Logic Synthesis
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Integrated Circuits, Technologies and Applications (ICTA)
abstract: Approximate circuits sacrificing accuracy in exchange for energy efficiency have been widely used in hardware deployment of neural networks (NNs). Approximate logic synthesis (ALS) has attracted attention due to its high efficiency in designing approximate circuits. This paper proposes a hybrid ALS based energy-efficient approximate multiplication and accumulation (MAC) unit, in which multipliers are designed by XOR-based BMF while adders are designed by CGP. Experiments show that compared to exact MAC, the proposed approximate MAC can reduce the power delay product (PDP) by 59.02% while the accuracy loss is only 0.72% in CIFAR10 using ResNet-18 and 2.22% in CIFAR100 using ResNet-50.

articleTitle: Optimization of Electrical Performance of aingaZnO Thin-Film Transistors by Interfacial Modification and Passivation
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Integrated Circuits, Technologies and Applications (ICTA)
abstract: Amorphous InGaZnO thin-film transistors (a-IGZO TFTs) exhibit superior performance than silicon and even polycrystalline silicon thin-film transistors, which have been widely investigated. This study utilizes two strategies to further optimize the electrical performance of a-IGZO TFTs. First, an AlO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">x</inf> layer is deposited on top of TFTs for passivation, which significantly improves the charge transport in transistors by preventing the dissociation of H<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>O and O<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> into active layer. Second, an ultrathin SiO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> layer is deposited between a-IGZO and gate dielectric for the interfacial modification, resulting in remarkably improved device uniformity. Additionally, near-ideal TFTs are realized, well fitted by theoretical simulation.

articleTitle: A 1.2-mA Fast-Charge Input Buffer with CLS for 4-MS/s SC Oversampling ADC Achieving +1-2.5-ppm/FSR INL
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Integrated Circuits, Technologies and Applications (ICTA)
abstract: This paper presents a 1.2-mA fast-charge input buffer with correlated level shifting (CLS) for a 4-MS/s SC oversampling ADC fabricated in 180-nm CMOS. The buffer includes a separate closed-loop fast charger to avoid the slewing process before the fine settling and CLS to confine the OTA's output into a small voltage range for linearity improvement with acceptable power consumption. The ADC with the buffer achieves 103.4-dB SNDR, 113.2-dB SFDR, and +/-2.5-ppm/FSR INL under 4-MS/s <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\boldsymbol{f}_{\mathbf{s}}$</tex>.

articleTitle: A 16MHz RC Oscillator with a Frequency Inaccuracy of 24ppm/°C from −40°C to 125°C Adopting Only Positive Temperature Coefficient Resistors
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Integrated Circuits, Technologies and Applications (ICTA)
abstract: A relaxation oscillator adopting only positive temperature coefficient resistors is presented in this paper. Two resistors with positive temperature coefficients are utilized to compensate for the resistance temperature drift by making the charging initial voltage of RC circuit follow the value change of the resistor in the charging branch. Designed in a 40nm CMOS process, the proposed RC relaxation oscillator operates at 16MHz, with a frequency inaccuracy of 24ppm/°C from -40°C to 125°C, and a power consumption of 3.125nW/kHz.

articleTitle: A 0.9V 1.2GHz-BW 15.8dBm-OIP3 Current Mode Analog Baseband for Broadband Receivers in 12nm FinFET CMOS
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Integrated Circuits, Technologies and Applications (ICTA)
abstract: This paper presents a wideband and high linearity current mode analog baseband(CMAB) designed for broadband RF receivers. The CMAB consists of a shunt feedback low pass filter and a wideband current amplifier based on cascode current mirror, incorporating gm-boosting technique and positive feedback capacitance reusing the identical boost amplifier, employing in broadband receivers using full current mode signal transmission. Fabricated in 12 nm FinFET CMOS process, the CMAB achieves an impressive 1dB-bandwidth of 1.2 GHz, a current gain of 19.2 dB and an OIP3 of 15.8 dBm, while consuming a low power of 20.3 mW with a supply voltage of only 0.9 V. The simulated performance demonstrates that this analog baseband satisfactorily fulfills the requirements for broadband zero-IF RF receivers, successfully overcoming the linearity limitations associated with low supply voltages and maximizing the benefits of FinFET technology when signal transmission in current mode.

articleTitle: MSeg-SLAM: A Semantic Visual SLAM System for Dynamic Scenes
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Integrated Circuits, Technologies and Applications (ICTA)
abstract: Visual Simultaneous Localization and Mapping (VSLAM) technique is crucial for intelligent mobile devices to acquire their current position and pose information. The traditional VSLAM system assumes that all objects in the environment are static by default. But in the physical world, some dynamic objects like humans are unavoidable, which imposes a huge burden on the system. This work proposes a semantic VSLAM system named MSeg-SLAM, which combines the VSLAM system and MSeg semantic segmentation network to reduce the impact of dynamic objects. At the same time, we generate semantic octree maps to optimize the storage space occupied by the dense point cloud map. Compared with the original ORB-SLAM2 system, the absolute trajectory error (ATE) can be reduced by over 93% in high dynamic scenes of the public TUM dataset. The results indicate our system has strong robustness and stability both in datasets and real-world practical applications.

articleTitle: Sufficient Hydroxylation Surface-Activation for Low-Temperature Glass/Glass Direct Bonding
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Integrated Circuits, Technologies and Applications (ICTA)
abstract: Glass/glass bonding, as an important technology to realize Co-Packaged Optics (CPO), is expected to be applied in data centers and high-performance computer manufacturing processes to improve computing speed and bandwidth. Low-temperature bonding is necessary for heterogeneous integration of photonic integrated circuits and application-specific integrated circuits. In this paper, Sulfuric/Peroxide Mix (SPM) solution and NaOH solution were used to hydrophilize the glass surfaces, and a water auxiliary layer was used to achieve glass/glass bonding with high bonding area and strength at 200°C. The bonding interface has a complete structure and excellent light transmittance. NaOH can hydrophilize and soften the surface through dissolution. The introduction of the water auxiliary layer can realize sufficient hydroxylation of the surface and reduce the bonding pressure through the surface tension and oxidize the unsaturated Si to promote gap closure. This article develops a simple and reliable method for glass/glass bonding.

articleTitle: Millimeter-Wave AlGaN/GaN MIS-HEMTs with Multiple T-Gate Technology
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Integrated Circuits, Technologies and Applications (ICTA)
abstract: We demonstrate the first Millimeter-Wave AlGaN/GaN MIS high-electron-mobility transistors (HEMTs) with Multiple T-gate technology. Thanks to the oxide layer formed by N<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>O plasma In-situ oxidation, the devices exhibit a low leakage current (10–6 mA/mm), a high on/off current ratio of 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">9</sup>. Multiple T-gate pattern mitigates electric-field crowding at the gate region by TCAD simulation, leading to a suppressed current collapse (~7.3%). Compare to conventional T-gate devices, Multiple T-gate devices have an improved frequency characteristic, which can be attributed to improved two dimensional electron gas (2DEG) mobility by 9.7%. The small signal measurement demonstrates that the Multiple T-gate devices can yield f<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">T</inf> and f<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">max</inf> of 87 GHz and 158 GHz, respectively. This paper revealing the great potential of Multiple T-gate GaN devices in high frequency applications.

articleTitle: A 16.5 mW 4.0 GHz Bandwidth VGA Based on Capacitance Neutralization Technique in 65 nm CMOS
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Integrated Circuits, Technologies and Applications (ICTA)
abstract: This paper presents a wideband variable gain amplifier (VGA) based on capacitance neutralization technique for high-speed communications and high-resolution radar systems. The negative capacitance path proposed in this paper effectively compensates the output capacitance of the VGA, thus achieving the bandwidth extension. Furthermore, it ensures a flat gain over a wide bandwidth at different gain settings. The VGA is designed in a standard 65nm CMOS process. The simulation results demonstrate that the VGA achieves a -3dB bandwidth of more than 4.0 GHz with a wide gain range from -2.8 to 49.4 dB. Moreover, it consumes 16.5 mW at a supply voltage of 1 V and has a core circuit area of 0.006mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>.

articleTitle: A 0/-5V High-Voltage Driver with Non-Overlapping Inverted Outputs in 65-nm CMOS Technology
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Integrated Circuits, Technologies and Applications (ICTA)
abstract: In this paper, a 0/-5V high-voltage driver with non-overlapping inverted outputs is designed. The output stage circuit not only achieves dead-time control of the two control signals for each driver, but also provides non-overlapping inverted outputs on chip with sufficient drive capability. The work is implemented in 65-nm CMOS technology and achieves a total delay of 4.82 ns at a working frequency of 10 MHz, with a rising time of 2.15 ns and a falling time of 2.01 ns.

articleTitle: Spice-Compatible Modeling of Double Barrier MTJ for Highly Reliable Circuits
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Integrated Circuits, Technologies and Applications (ICTA)
abstract: This paper proposes a compact model of tungsten (W) engineered perpendicular magnetic tunnel junction (p-MTJ) with double CoFeB/MgO interfaces for circuit design. Reliability issues, such as process variation and stochastic switching, have been considered to enhance the accuracy of the model, rendering it approaching the reality application scenarios. A STT-MRAM memory circuit is simulated by using this model to investigate the writing and reading performance. With the benefits brought by W to p-MTJ, the circuit demonstrates less writing energy and higher reading reliability, owing to the enhanced perpendicular anisotropy and high tunnel magneto resistance ratio.

articleTitle: A Fully Integrated High-Efficiency All-NMOS Charge Pump for Wide Input Range Ultra-Low Dropout Regulator
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Integrated Circuits, Technologies and Applications (ICTA)
abstract: This paper presents an auto-configurable multistage charge pump (CP) designed for a wide input range NMOS low dropout regulator (LDO). The proposed CP built in all-NMOS with multi-gate-boost driver improves the terrible conduct resistance at near-threshold voltage. The CP is also adaptively cascaded, so that the proposed LDO can meet the requirements of wide input range, large loading range and low dropout voltage. With 1.1V input and 420μA loading, the simulation results show the proposed CP reaches 90.5% and 56.1% peak efficiencies for one- and four-stage configurations, respectively. A prototype NMOS LDO with proposed CP has been fabricated in 0.18μm BCD technology. The experimental results show that with 1.1~6.5V input range, the CP can generate a 4.0~10.0V power rail to drive the gate of the power transistor, and a 3.0~5.5V power rail for the control part.

articleTitle: Simple-Logic Comparator-Offset Mitigation Technique for Resistor-Based Temperature Sensor in DFLL
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Integrated Circuits, Technologies and Applications (ICTA)
abstract: We propose a simple-logic system-level comparator offset mitigation technique for the resistor-based temperature sensor implemented with a digital frequency-locked loop (DFLL). Knowing that the frequency error due to the comparator offset depends on the initial digital-controlled oscillator's frequency (f<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">DCO</inf>), we can preset the initial f<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">DCO</inf> and obtain the average of the locked frequencies to eliminate the frequency and thus temperature error. The entire scheme entails only simple logics, minimizing the area overhead associated with the offset-calibration circuit. We verify the technique with a DFLL resistor-based temperature sensor designed in a 65-nm CMOS process. The simulated temperature error is <±0.4°C over a temperature range of -40 to 125°C in the presence of ±10mV comparator offset.

articleTitle: A Lightweight Stereo Matching Neural Network Based on Depthwise Separable Convolution
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Integrated Circuits, Technologies and Applications (ICTA)
abstract: Deep learning-based stereo matching methods have significantly improved the accuracy of disparity maps. However, they also pose challenges such as increased computational complexity and redundant model parameters, which hinder deployment on resource-constrained devices. To overcome this challenge, this paper introduces depthwise separable convolution to decompose the 3D convolution and analyzes the computational overhead corresponding to different decomposition orders of 3D convolutions. By strategically selecting the decomposition block with the lower computational cost during network construction, we effectively reduce the computational requirements of the feature extraction and cost aggregation modules. Experimental results show that our lightweight network model achieves a 41% reduction in computational requirements and a 36% reduction in parameters compared to the baseline model, while maintaining comparable accuracy. This demonstrates its competitiveness against other state-of-the-art models.

articleTitle: A 1.76 fj/Conv 1.49µW 12-Bit SAR ADC with Coarse and Fine Quantization for Implantable BCI Applications
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Integrated Circuits, Technologies and Applications (ICTA)
abstract: This paper presents a 12-bit SAR ADC designed for implantable BCI applications. The proposed SAR ADC utilizes the low-power and high-precision comparators for the coarse and fine quantization respectively to achieve optimal tradeoffs between ENOB and power consumption. A hybrid coding (thermometer and binary) scheme is deployed to further save power consumption. The proposed SAR ADC works at 0.6 V, and achieves a 70.2 dB SNDR, with a power consumption of 1.49 µW. Additionally, it attains a Figure-of-Merit (FOM) of 1.76 fj/step and occupies only 0.00612 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> in a 40nm CMOS process.

articleTitle: A Output Code Density Histograms Based Calibration Algorithm of Capacitor Mismatch for SAR ADC
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Integrated Circuits, Technologies and Applications (ICTA)
abstract: A scheme for the calibration of capacitor mismatch in a successive-approximation register (SAR) analog-to-digital converter (ADC), using output code density histograms, is presented. By iterating the actual weights to minimize the residual standard deviation (RSD) between the partial fitting curve and the reference curve that corresponds to an ideal ADC, the performance of ADC is improved without any additional analog circuitry. Measurement results demonstrate that the signal-to-noise distortion ratio (SNDR) can be increased from 65.62 dB to 67.39 dB, and the spurious-free dynamic range (SFDR) from 77.26 dB to 87.41 dB at 1MHz input frequency, with a sampling frequency of 50 MS/s.

articleTitle: A Miniaturized Flexible Optoelectronic System for Implantable Fluorescence Sensing
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Integrated Circuits, Technologies and Applications (ICTA)
abstract: Fluorescent sensors have attracted extensive attention in brain-computer interfaces due to their high specificity and sensitivity. Here, a miniaturized optoelectronic system capable of fluorescence sensing, signal processing, and wireless communication is presented. The system consists of a thin-film probe for neurochemical sensing and a compact flexible circuit as a control unit, with a total dimension of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbf{0.8}\times \mathbf{0.85}\times \mathbf{0.1}\ \mathbf{cm}^{\mathbf{3}}$</tex> and a weight of 0.18 g. The system has been applied to dopamine sensing in human serum with a sensitivity of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbf{1.22}\ \boldsymbol{\mu} \mathbf{A}/\boldsymbol{\mu}\mathbf{M}$</tex>, a detection limit of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbf{0.1}\ \boldsymbol{\mu} \mathbf{M}$</tex>, and a deviation of less than 7.3%, leading to great promise in implantable biomedical applications.

articleTitle: Towards Efficient On-Chip Learning for Spiking Neural Networks Accelerator with Surrogate Gradient
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Integrated Circuits, Technologies and Applications (ICTA)
abstract: Spiking Neural Networks (SNNs) have advantages in low power consumption, however, there is a problem of non-differentiability in the backpropagation (BP) of SNN. In this work, we propose a high-performance, low-cost SNN accelerator supports on-chip learning and utilizes a surrogate gradient (SG) for supervised learning, addressing the non-differentiability issue. The design is implemented on the VC707 FPGA, operating at a clock frequency of 115 MHz with a power consumption of 798 mW, achieving an accuracy of 95.49% on the MNIST dataset. The training and inference speeds are 1183 frame/s and 4163 frame/s. The training energy is 0.67 mJ/img and the inference energy is 0.21 mJ/img, reducing the energy consumption by 10–40 times compared to state-of-the-art (SOTA) unsupervised works.

articleTitle: Low-Power Inductor-Less Optical Receiver for 50G PON in 28nm CMOS
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Integrated Circuits, Technologies and Applications (ICTA)
abstract: This paper proposes a low-power inductorless optical receiver for 50G PON optical network unit in 28nm CMOS. A feedforward-structure TIA is utilized with a trans-impedance gain of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbf{50}\mathbf{dB}\mathbf{\Omega}$</tex>, which is almost doubled compared to the single-stage TIA with the same bandwidth. With energy efficiency of 0.34pJ/bit, the whole receiver achieves a trans-impedance gain of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbf{74.6}\mathbf{dB}\mathbf{\Omega}$</tex> with equivalent input noise current of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbf{3.14} \boldsymbol{\mu} \mathbf{Arms}$</tex> and input noise density of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbf{20.3}\ \mathbf{pA}/\sqrt{\text{Hz}}$</tex>.

articleTitle: A 160nA Quiescent Current and 97.0% Peak Efficiency AOT Buck Converter With Adaptive Dead-Time Control
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Integrated Circuits, Technologies and Applications (ICTA)
abstract: This paper presents a 160 nA quiescent current adaptive on-time (AOT) dc-dc buck converter with a wide load range for ultra-low power application. The dynamic-bias and adaptive-bias techniques are utilized to reduce the total quiescent current. The AOT and three modes of control technologies are designed to realized the higher efficiency compared with conventional voltage and current mode control. An adaptive dead-time controller is proposed to improve the efficiency of the proposed buck converter. It was implemented in a 22 nm CMOS technology. The simulation results show the converter can achieve a 97.0% peak efficiency and the efficiencies can be greater than 88% from 20 µA to 1 A in the whole input range. The input voltage ranges from 1.8-3.6 V and output voltage is 1.4 V for 1 µA to 1 A (1000,000X) load range.

articleTitle: Design of An Asymmetrical Pseudo-Doherty Load-Modulated Balanced Amplifier with 15-dB Back-Off High Efficiency
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Integrated Circuits, Technologies and Applications (ICTA)
abstract: This paper designs an asymmetrical pseudo-Doherty load-modulated balanced amplifier (APD-LMBA) with 15-dB back-off high efficiency. Theoretical analysis reveals the output back-off (OBO) can be extended by appropriately controlling the power ratios and the bias voltages between the control amplifier (CA) and the balanced amplifiers (BAs). To validate the analysis, a 2.5-2.9 GHz APD-LMBA is designed, simulated and measured. Experimental results show that the APD-LMBA achieves drain efficiency (DE) of 69.8% - 78.9% at saturation, 46% - 60% at 6-dB back-off, 42% - 57% at 10-dB back-off, and 34% - 47% at 15-dB back-off across the band.

articleTitle: A High-Linearity, Energy-Efficient Switched-Capacitor Computing Circuit for Edge Applications
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Integrated Circuits, Technologies and Applications (ICTA)
abstract: This paper presents a passive switched-capacitor multiplication circuit for deep neural network computing in edge applications. A novel capacitor switching scheme is proposed to eliminate the computation error caused by non-binary-weighted parasitic capacitance, and dramatically increase the computing accuracy. It also simplifies the switching sequences to five phases to reduce the computation latency and improve the energy efficiency. Additionally, a mixed-signal multiply-add computing array is built with nine proposed switched-capacitor circuits and a SAR ADC. The simulation results in 28-nm technology show that the proposed array can achieve an energy efficiency of 11.94 TOPS/W and an average absolute computation error of 0.25 LSB, resulting in a classification accuracy of 98.43% when used for a 3-layer neural network on the MNIST dataset. As compared to the state-of-art mixed-signal computing circuit, the proposed circuit can enhance 1.19× energy efficiency and reduce 74% average absolute computation error.

articleTitle: An FPGA-Based Efficient NTT Accelerator for Post-Quantum Cryptography CRYSTALS-Kyber
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Integrated Circuits, Technologies and Applications (ICTA)
abstract: CRYSTALS-Kyber has emerged as a significant lattice-based post-quantum cryptography (PQC) scheme. As one of the four finalists at round three in NIST's PQC standardization, CRYSTALS-Kyber uses number theoretic transform (NTT) to optimize polynomial multiplication, which is the most complex operation in CRYSTALS-Kyber. This work proposes an FPGA-based efficient NTT accelerator with a novel butterfly unit and an efficient modular polynomial multiplier. This work adopts a radix-4-based configurable NTT design, which can achieve forward and inverse NTT operations on a unified architecture. The proposed architecture on the Xilinx Virtex-7 FPGA platform is 1.5x faster than the traditional radix-4 NTT architecture and 2.3x faster than the traditional radix-2 NTT architecture.

articleTitle: An Efficient Hardware Implementation of Dilated Convolution Using a Novel Channel-Equivalent Decomposition Method
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Integrated Circuits, Technologies and Applications (ICTA)
abstract: This paper proposes an efficient hardware deployment method for dilated convolution, and designs a novel channel-equivalent decomposition method for dilated convolution to fully utilize the effective data in the dilated convolution, significantly reducing the redundant zero operation requirement in the dilated convolution, greatly reducing memory bandwidth requirements, and improving throughput. The efficient dilated convolution operation unit is implemented on the Xilinx ZCU102 FPGA, with a working frequency of 333MHz. The test results indicate that the performance of running the dilated convolution layer of VGG-SSD is 192GOPS. At a power consumption of 2.1W, the average energy efficiency of the system is 91.4GOPS/W.

articleTitle: Design Considerations of Multi-Level 1S1R Cell for In-Memory Computing
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Integrated Circuits, Technologies and Applications (ICTA)
abstract: In this paper, we focus on the exploration of the multi-level 1S1R cell for in-memory computing (IMC). We develop Verilog-A behavior models for both the selector and resistive random-access memory (RRAM) to assess the influence of voltage shift, non-linearity, and selectivity on the performance of 1S1R-based IMC. Our study aims to provide guidance for integrating a multi-level 1S1R crossbar array for in-memory computing applications.

articleTitle: A 250-kHz-BW 15.8-ENOB 2nd-Order Noise-Shaping SAR ADC With Multi-Path-Input Floating Inverter Amplifier
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Integrated Circuits, Technologies and Applications (ICTA)
abstract: This paper presents a power-efficient 2<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">nd</sup>-order noise-shaping (NS) successive approximation register (SAR) analog-to-digital converter (ADC) in which the comparator is implemented with a multi-path-input floating inverter amplifier (MPI FIA). Thanks to the merits of FIA this comparator can lower the NS-SAR ADC noise and power, and improve its robustness against process, voltage and temperature (PVT) variation. A 12-bit NS-SAR ADC with this comparator is implemented in 180-nm CMOS process. The simulation results show that, with a 250-kHz bandwidth and an over-sampling ratio (OSR) of 10, the SAR ADC achieves 97.15-dB signal-to-noise-and-distortion ratio (SNDR) and consumes only 3.76 mW under the 3.3-V power supply, which leads to an Schreier figure-of-merit (FoMs) of 175.4 dB.

articleTitle: A Novel Dual-Polarized Filtering Magneto-Electric Dipole Antenna Without Extra Filtering Circuits
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Integrated Circuits, Technologies and Applications (ICTA)
abstract: A novel dual-polarized filtering magneto-electric dipole antenna (MEDA) is proposed in this paper. The MEDA has an intrinsic radiation null, a pair of U-stubs are designed to enhance the gain suppression of the intrinsic null. By etching C-slots on the electric dipoles, an integrated radiation null is generated. This null, together with the intrinsic null of MEDA, achieves a bandpass filtering response. The simulated results show that the impedance bandwidth is 23.63% (24.78-31.42 GHz) and the 3-dB gain bandwidth is 58.10% (18.26-33.21 GHz) with an average gain of 8.5 dBi is achieved. The radiation suppression level of radiation nulls is more than 20 dB.

articleTitle: Graph Neural Network Assisted S-Parameter Inference and Control-Word Generation of Terahertz Reconfigurable Intelligent Surface
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Integrated Circuits, Technologies and Applications (ICTA)
abstract: For large-scale terahertz (THz) reconfigurable intelligent surfaces (RIS), each unit element is supposed to be controlled by an independent voltage source. This leads to a huge solution space for both key metrics inference and control-word generation. In this paper, we propose a fast AI-assisted control-word generation scheme to reduce the computation cost of Electro-Magnetic (EM) simulations (Forward Model) and to accelerate the iteration process for control word search (Inverse Model). The results demonstrate that the Forward Model can predict the S-parameters between 100GHz and 800GHz with a minimal mean absolute error (MAE) of 0.69dB. Our method is more than 180 times faster than traditional full-wave simulation methods without training time. Additionally, the Inverse Model can generate demanded control words within 1.5 dB error requirement in less than 200 iterations.

articleTitle: Fast and Accurate Alignment and Bonding System Based on Advanced Packaging Technology
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Integrated Circuits, Technologies and Applications (ICTA)
abstract: In the semiconductor packaging production line, with the increasing integration of chips, the size and pitch of solder joints are decreasing, which puts high demands on the alignment process. Especially with the emergence of chiplet and die-to-wafer technology, high-precision and high-speed alignment technology has become popular. In this paper, based on some image processing schemes, we propose a machine vision algorithm for realizing high-precision and high-speed flip chip bonding, and a flip chip bonding system is then constructed. Finally, the idea for the realization of the die-to-wafer bonding system is discussed.

articleTitle: A 128×128 15µm-Pitch DROIC with Pixel-Level 14-Bit ADC
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Integrated Circuits, Technologies and Applications (ICTA)
abstract: Digital readout integrated circuits (DROIC) show advantages in infrared imaging scenarios with large charge capacity and wide dynamic range. In this paper, a 128×128 DROIC in 15µm pitch size is proposed, which implements 14bit pixel-level analog-to-digital converter (ADC). The design is based on 65nm 1P9M CMOS process. The chip size is 2.6mm×3.2mm. According to the simulation results, the non-linearity is 0.6%. At frequency of 100×7/128, the signal to noise and distortion ratio (SNDR) of pixel achieves 50dB. The typical power consumption of the proposed array is 33mW and the charge handling capacity is 4.6Ge<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-</sup>.

articleTitle: Experiments and Hygrothermal Stress Analysis for a QFN Package
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Integrated Circuits, Technologies and Applications (ICTA)
abstract: In this study, the material parameters of EMC related to moisture diffusion, thermo-mechanical behaviors were tested experimentally. A typical QFN with moisture absorption was simulated and the hygrothermal stresses in the package during reflow or thermal cycling were analyzed by Comsol. The effects of chip location and pad grooves were studied. The results show that the hygrothermal stress in the package was near the interfaces, which is much larger at the highest and lowest temperatures. The area of high stress will shift with the locations of the chip. The pad grooves reduce the average stress at the interfaces, but increase the risks of local damages near the tips of grooves.

articleTitle: ACCLAIM: An End-to-End SystemC-AMS Simulation Framework for Analog In-Memory-Computing
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Integrated Circuits, Technologies and Applications (ICTA)
abstract: This paper presents ACCLAIM, a novel framework based on SystemC-AMS for evaluating nonidealities in crossbar-based Analog In-Memory-Computing, offering a comprehensive and efficient alternative to SPICE-level simulations and analytical behavior-level simulators. ACCLAIM covers the end-to-end computing process. The dataflow of ACCLAIM is investigated and the accumulative effect of nonidealities is analyzed. Accuracy evaluation of LeNet is discussed based on the dataflow simulation.

articleTitle: Error Bits Recovering in 3D NAND Flash Memory: A Novel State-Shift Re-Program (SRP) Scheme
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Integrated Circuits, Technologies and Applications (ICTA)
abstract: To address serious concerns on charge-loss-related data retention in charge-trap (CT) 3D NAND flash memory, a novel state-shift re-program (SRP) scheme is proposed to recover error bits after long-term retention. Different from traditional re-program methods, the proposed scheme can avoid the degradation of low-state error bits significantly, and could proceed with no need to invoke the original data file. Based on the characterizations of TLC (3bit/cell) 3D NAND chip on a high-speed NAND chip tester, it is shown that the proposed SRP scheme can recover <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbf{20}\sim\mathbf{30}\%$</tex> error bits in the cycled blocks with a large amount of error bits.

articleTitle: High Energy-Efficient Approximate In-SRAM Computing with Bit-Wise Compressor Configuration and Data-Aware Weight Remapping Method for Neural Network Acceleration
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Integrated Circuits, Technologies and Applications (ICTA)
abstract: This paper proposes an approximate SRAM based computing-in-memory (SRAM-CIM) macro for energy-efficient multiplication-and-accumulation (MAC) operations. Utilizing the error resilience property of NNs, the compressor configuration for each weight bit is presented for high energy and area efficiency. Meanwhile, a data-aware weight remapping method is proposed to further improve the NN accuracy without additional retraining process. Experimental results show that our proposed approximate SRAM-CIM macro can achieve 35.5% higher energy efficiency, 8.71% lower area, and 48.4% higher energy efficiency per unit area, compared to previous approximate SRAM-CIM design while maintaining similar NN accuracy.

articleTitle: A 16-Bit 18-MSPS SAR ADC with Hybrid Synchronous and Asynchronous Control Logic
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Integrated Circuits, Technologies and Applications (ICTA)
abstract: This paper presents a 16-bit, 18-MSPS SAR ADC utilizing hybrid synchronous and asynchronous (HYSAS) timing control logic based on an on-chip delay-locked loop (DLL). The HYSAS scheme can provide a longer CDAC settling time than the synchronous and asynchronous SAR ADC. Therefore, the issue of incomplete settling or ringing in the DAC voltage for cases of either on-chip or off-chip reference voltage can be solved to a large extent. In addition, the foreground calibration of the CDAC's mismatch is performed with an FIR-BPF based LMS algorithm in an off-chip FPGA. Fabricated in 40-nm CMOS, the prototype ADC achieves 94.02-dB SFDR, and 75.98-dB SNDR for a 2.88-MHz input under 18-MSPS sampling rate.

articleTitle: A 400uW 3.6GHz-4.6GHz Low Power Cryogenic CP-PLL with Transformer-Based VCO in 28nm Bulk CMOS
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Integrated Circuits, Technologies and Applications (ICTA)
abstract: A 400uW 3.6GHz - 4.6GHz low power interger-N CP-PLL working down to 3.5K is proposed for quantum applications. It has minimal power consumption owing to its utilization of a source-switching charge pump, coupled with a low current bias transformer-based VCO that ensures enough output amplitude. The proposed PLL is fabricated in 28-nm Bulk CMOS process. Under 3.5K temperature, the PLL achieves 2.17ps jitter @4GHz with -70 reference spur consuming only 400uW power consumption and the FOM is -237dBc/Hz.

articleTitle: A 325 FPS Corner-Detection Accelerator with Hardware-Oriented Optimization
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Integrated Circuits, Technologies and Applications (ICTA)
abstract: Simultaneous Localization and Mapping(SLAM) is an important technology in robot positioning and navigation. In visual odometry, the extraction accuracy and efficiency of corner detection directly affects the performance of the system. However, due to the complexity of corner detection algorithms, it is difficult to meet the requirements of real-time, efficient, and low-cost simultaneously, especially on robots. GFTT corner detection based on Harris has good performance in accuracy. However, hardware implementation increases computational complexity and resource consumption. In this work, an optimized corner detection accelerator is proposed to replace GFTT, which is hardware-friendly to be implemented on edge embedded devices. Without significant loss of accuracy, its computational complexity and hardware resource consumption are greatly reduced, and it can be good candidate for FPGA and ASIC designs. The detection image frame rate can reach 325 fps that outperforms the previous works.

articleTitle: Highly Linear Receiver Analog Front-end for High-speed Optical Communication
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Integrated Circuits, Technologies and Applications (ICTA)
abstract: This paper presents a <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\boldsymbol{4}\times \boldsymbol{112}\mathbf{Gb}/\mathbf{s}$</tex> four-level pulse amplitude modulation (PAM-4) receiver analog front-end design implemented using the 90nm SiGe BiCMOS process. To address the dynamic range requirements of the input current, a novel variable gain amplifier based on a double Gilbert cell is introduced. Experimental measurements demonstrate that the optical receiver front-end achieves a maximum transimpedance gain of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\boldsymbol{74}\mathbf{dB}\mathbf{\Omega}$</tex>, a bandwidth of 32GHz, and a total harmonic distortion (THD) below 5% for input currents up to 3mApp.

articleTitle: Simulation for the Feasibility of IGZO Channel in 3D Vertical FeFET Memory Based on TCAD
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Integrated Circuits, Technologies and Applications (ICTA)
abstract: To get insight into the feasibility of the In-Ga-Zn-O (IGZO) channel in 3D vertical ferroelectric field effect transistor (FeFET), the device performance comparison with traditional Si and poly-Si channel are systematical investigated based on 3D TCAD simulation including the effects of channel length, ferroelectric layer thickness, and temperature. It reveals that the devices with Si channel have lower subthreshold swing and poly-Si has higher memory window under most conditions, while the device with IGZO channel has lower off current at high temperature.

articleTitle: C-band 60W GaN Power Amplifier MMIC with over 53% Efficiency
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Integrated Circuits, Technologies and Applications (ICTA)
abstract: In order to adapt to the development, a 60W power amplifier microwave monolithic integrated circuit (MMIC) with an operating frequency of 5.2-6.2 GHz is designed for C-band radar systems. The harmonics suppression characteristics of the proposed power amplifier are improved by adopting inductor-capacitor resonance in the output matching network. The size of the power amplifier MMIC is <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\boldsymbol{3.6}\times \boldsymbol{4.1}\ \mathbf{mm^{2}}$</tex>. The measured results show that the output power is greater than 60 W, the power gain is 20 dB, the harmonics suppression are greater than 45 dB, and the power additional efficiency (PAE) is higher than 53%, under the verification condition of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\boldsymbol{50}\ \boldsymbol{\mu}\mathbf{s}$</tex> pulse width and 5% duty cycle. The characteristics of the power amplifier proposed in this paper are beneficial for miniaturization of radar transceiver systems.

articleTitle: A Lightweight Integer-STBP On-Chip Learning Method of Spiking Neural Networks For Edge Processors
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Integrated Circuits, Technologies and Applications (ICTA)
abstract: Spiking Neural Networks (SNNs) with energy-efficient on neuromorphic hardware are suitable for edge processors with limited resources. The software-hardware co-design plays a crucial role in achieving optimal performance in such processors. Current research focuses on equipping edge processors with on-chip learning capabilities, and a high accuracy low hardware requirements on-chip learning algorithm is needed. Spatio-Temporal BackPropagation (STBP) algorithm enables deep-layer SNNs and high-accuracy training, shows great potential as an on-chip learning algorithm. However, the high computational complexity and storage requirements of STBP making edge processors design extremely challenging. Despite the efforts and significant progress made by many studies, the complex calculations required for surrogate gradient and the high storage requirements for membrane potentials still limit deployment. This work proposes a lightweight integer-STBP on-chip training method of SNNs for edge processors with lightweight surrogate gradients and low-storage computation flow, significantly reducing computational complexity and storage requirements. Experimental shows that, the proposed method achieve the same accuracy as state-of-the-art method while reducing the operations without MAC to 66% and storage requirements to 22%.

articleTitle: INVITED PAPER: A 4.5-5.4GHz Digital Bang-Bang PLL for Cryogenic Applications
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Integrated Circuits, Technologies and Applications (ICTA)
abstract: This paper introduces a 4.5G~5.4GHz digital bang-bang PLL for 77K cryogenic applications. The digital approach overcomes the design challenges that arise from a wide temperature operation range. The implicit common-mode resonance in the DCO suppresses flicker noise up-conversion. Fabricated in a 40nm CMOS process, the PLL achieves -132 dBc/Hz phase noise at 10MHz offset and an integrated jitter of 295fs at 77K while consuming a low power of 2.5mW.

articleTitle: Invited Paper: A Memristor-Based Stateful Majority-Inverter Graph Logic and 1-Bit Full Adder for In-Memory Computing Systems
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Integrated Circuits, Technologies and Applications (ICTA)
abstract: This paper proposes a new non-destructive stateful Majority-Inverter Graph (MIG) logic scheme based on bipolar memristors. The proposed MIG logic scheme can be executed natively in memristor arrays, taking advantage of its non-destructive and stateful features to facilitate logic cascades and the realization of complex logic and arithmetic functions. The implementation of the 1-bit full adder requires only a simple application of a sequence voltage, which is experimentally verified in a 1t1r array, demonstrating high computational efficiency, and the logic operation power consumption is calculated and analyzed in detail. This work presents a stateful MIG logic implementation approach at the array level, providing a powerful logic primitive for building in-memory computing systems in the future.

articleTitle: Cyclical Progress in Design and Technology
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Integrated Circuits, Technologies and Applications (ICTA)
abstract: Progress in engineering systems is the result of the combined improvements of technology and design methods. It is often a cyclic process, stimulated by success and failure. When the innovation loop stalls in producing effective progress, a change in paradigm is needed. Many examples populate the history of science and engineering, as well as of mankind.

articleTitle: A 12bit 160MS/s Pipelined SAR ADC with a MOS Self-Biased Cascoded Ring Amplifier
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Integrated Circuits, Technologies and Applications (ICTA)
abstract: In this design, a new structure of ring amplifier (RA) is proposed to meet high-speed applications, which uses low threshold voltage transistors to increase the charge rate for capacitors. The stability is ensured by increasing the dead-zone voltage using series-connected transistors. In this design, it is utilized as an inter-stage amplifier in a 160 MS/s, 12 bits pipelined successive approximation (pipeline SAR) analog-to-digital converter (ADC). The pipeline SAR ADC is designed with a 55 nm CMOS process and occupies an overall chip area of 500 × 170 µm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>. Without calibration, the dynamic performance of ADC achieves 58.56 dB for SNDR and 69.14 dB for SFDR.

articleTitle: A Transformer-Based End-to-End Network for Unmanned Aerial Vehicle Aerial Image Object Detection
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Integrated Circuits, Technologies and Applications (ICTA)
abstract: The Transformer-based end-to-end networks have received extensive attention from the academia and industry due to their superior detection performance and elimination of handcrafted components. However, their high computational costs have hindered their applicability in unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) aerial image object detection tasks driven by robotics technology. This paper proposes a novel Transformer-based end-to-end network, named Accelerated DETR, which significantly reduces computational costs while maintaining the advantages of the Transformer architecture, leading to improved detection accuracy. Experimental results demonstrate that Accelerated DETR achieves an impressive AP<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">50</inf> of 55.8 and operates at 40 FPS with only 41.6M network parameters.

articleTitle: An EEG Signal Processing System Design with Approximate Operations
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Integrated Circuits, Technologies and Applications (ICTA)
abstract: This paper presents an EEG signal processing system with an application to emotional recognition, which includes three primary modules: preprocessing, feature extraction, and emotion classification. A hardware stream control mode tailored for the system was devised to minimize redundant logic computations. Additionally, we used a piecewise linear approximation method for three non-linear operations utilized in the neural network (tanh activation function, sigmoid activation function, and square root function). The resulting hardware circuit achieves a dual-label classification of 16 emotions, with an average accuracy of 64.5% on the DEAP dataset. Compared to other state-of-art systems developed using DEAP dataset, this design exhibits superior real-time processing capabilities (latency of 0.02ms), while recognizing the maximum number of emotion classes without compromising additional power and area.

articleTitle: An 800MS/s 100MHz BW Continuous-Time Pipeline ADC with Integrator-filter and Digital Reconstruction Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Integrated Circuits, Technologies and Applications (ICTA)
abstract: This paper presents a two-stage continuous-time pipeline ADC with inherent anti-aliasing using Integrator-filter and digital reconstruction algorithm without dither injection. The proposed Integrator-filter exhibits better performance compared with the first-order and second-order low-pass filters, allowing larger inter-stage gain and dynamic range. Also, an algorithm without dither injection is presented to obtain the tap weights of the reconstruction filters. The presented ADC clocked at 800MHz achieves 79.4dB peak SNDR with 100MHz bandwidth in 65-nm CMOS and consumes 14.7 mW, resulting in a FOM<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">s</inf> of 177.7dB.

articleTitle: A 6.9-17.0 GHz Low-noise Amplifier in 65nm CMOS
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Integrated Circuits, Technologies and Applications (ICTA)
abstract: Due to the ever-increasing data transmission rate, the wideband LNAs are being required popularly. A wideband LNA operating at 6.9-17.0 GHz with two cascode amplification stages is proposed. Source inductance degeneration and Chebyshev filter matching are used to achieve low noise and wideband input matching simultaneously. The <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\Pi- \text{type}$</tex> inter-stage matching circuit is implemented to satisfy bandwidth requirements. Fabricated in 65nm CMOS, the amplifier finally obtained a gain of 19.7 dB and a minimum noise figure of 3.9 dB with good return loss and unconditional stability.

articleTitle: A Fast Bioimpedance Measurement Chip Design Using Dynamic Current
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Integrated Circuits, Technologies and Applications (ICTA)
abstract: This paper proposes a method of IC design for fast bioimpedance measurement. The implemented chip comprises a current steering digital-to-analog converter (DAC), a voltage comparator, and a logic control module. The chip dynamically drives current into the impedance to be test, and the corresponding DAC code is read when the output voltage crosses the threshold the voltage comparator. The chip was designed and fabricated using SMIC 180-nm CMOS process. The results demonstrate that an impedance measurement range from <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbf{200}\mathbf{\Omega}$</tex> to <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbf{80}\mathbf{k}\mathbf{\Omega}$</tex> is achieved within <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbf{10.2}\ \boldsymbol{\mu} \mathbf{s}$</tex> under a clock at 100 MHz.

articleTitle: High-Efficiency Class-B/F W-Band Balanced Frequency Sixtupler in GaN HEMT Technology
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Integrated Circuits, Technologies and Applications (ICTA)
abstract: This paper presents a W-band balanced frequency sixtupler in <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbf{0.12}\ \boldsymbol{\mu} \mathbf{m}$</tex> gallium nitride (GaN) HEMT technology, which is composed of a Marchand balun, a balanced Class-B doubler and a Class-F tripler. Leveraging the Class-F operation, the tripler efficiently extracts the third harmonic, generating an output waveform with quasi-square wave. The proposed sixtupler achieves a maximum output power of 6.12 dBm, a 3-dB bandwidth spaning from 90 to 94.2 GHz and a power efficiency of 22.9%. Moreover, the harmonics from the 1<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">st</sup> to the 5<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">th</sup> order are effectively suppressed by more than 20 dBc.

articleTitle: A Microfluidic Impedance Flow Cytometer for Highly Accurate Detection of Circulating Tumor Cells via Cellular Mechanical and Electrical Properties Sensing
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Integrated Circuits, Technologies and Applications (ICTA)
abstract: Microfluidic Impedance Cytometry (MIC) is a cuttingedge method for analyzing single cell that utilizes microfluidic technology and impedance sensing principles, which can be used for circulating tumor cells (CTCs) based cancer diagnostics. However, in practical applications, the impedance signal closely correlates with cell size, posing a challenge in detecting CTCs in blood, especially when CTC sizes resemble those of blood cells, potentially causing diagnostic errors. To tackle this issue, we propose an impedance-based CTC detection system with custom designed circuits, electrodes, and microfluidic chip that enable simultaneous extraction of mechanical and electrical properties of individual cells from processed electrical signals. Our system overcomes the challenge posed by the intrinsic relationship between impedance signals and cell sizes. We tested our system on A549 lung cancer cells, white blood cells, and red blood cells. The results show that the system could not only distinguish blood cells and CTCs with different sizes, but also accurately differentiate blood cells and CTCs with similar sizes.

articleTitle: A FinFET Integrated STT-MRAM with Triple Balanced Access Strategy
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Integrated Circuits, Technologies and Applications (ICTA)
abstract: The demand for area-efficient, low-power memory circuits is increasing exponentially with the development of wearable devices. Emerging FinFET technology drives STT-MRAM designs to better meet this need. However, comprehensive optimization of STT-MRAM circuits regarding power consumption, area, and sensing yield is still a severe challenge. This work focuses on a low-power, area-saving access strategy without sensing yield loss based on 1T1MTJ for STT-MRAM in FinFET technology. In this paper, FinFET-based MRAM bitcells are constructed, and the advantages of using FinFETs for MRAM design are analyzed. Moreover, a triple-balanced voltage sense amplifier (TB-VSA) for sensing 1T1MTJ is proposed, offering comprehensive optimization in area, power, and sensing yield. Simulation is performed based on 14-nm FinFET logic process. Monte Carlo (MC) simulation shows that the proposed sense amplifier exhibits excellent tolerance to PVT variations, and it achieves at least 47% energy and 35% area saving compared to previous works.

articleTitle: A Genuine-Equilibrium Monte Carlo Sampling-Based Effective Algorithm for Fully-Connected Ising Models
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Integrated Circuits, Technologies and Applications (ICTA)
abstract: Ising machines have emerged as a potential technique for hardware acceleration in solving combinatorial optimization problems. However, an effective and hardware-implementation-friendly algorithm is still required to further enhance the fully-connected Ising machine's performance. Parallel momentum-tempering (PMT) algorithm is proposed in this paper, incorporating the full parallel updating capability of momentum annealing (MA) with the global exploration in the solution space provided by parallel tempering (PT). PMT exhibits an excellent performance, and a PMT with 8 replicas surpasses MA on the WK2000 max-cut benchmark, achieving a considerable 80%(1k/6k) reduction in required iteration steps while obtaining a mean cut value of 33,160. Besides, PMT is well-matched for hardware implementation versus MA, benefiting from invariant parameters in each replica.

articleTitle: A 11 mV-Undershoot PT Controlled Buck Converter with Adaptive Pulse Train Generator
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Integrated Circuits, Technologies and Applications (ICTA)
abstract: This article presents a fast transient pulse train (PT)-controlled DC-DC buck converter over a wide output range. An adaptive pulse train generator (APTG) is proposed to improve the transient response. To achieve a wide power range, the buck converter operates in pseudo-continuous conduction mode (PCCM). PT-controlled buck converter is implemented in the 180 nm CMOS process. Simulation results show that, for a 300 mA current step, the undershoot and overshoot spikes are 11 mV and 16 mV, respectively. The transient recovery times are 6.1 <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mu \mathrm{s}$</tex> and 4.1 <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mu \mathrm{s}$</tex>, respectively. The buck converter has an output voltage range of 1-3.3 v providing a maximum load current of 1000 mA, and achieves a peak efficiency of 92.6% at 200-mA load current.

articleTitle: An FPGA-Based Low-Power Mobile-NetV2 Accelerator
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Integrated Circuits, Technologies and Applications (ICTA)
abstract: Convolutional neural networks (CNNs) have been widely recognized and applied in the field of robotics. However, the huge amount of computation and parameters of CNN bring great challenges to its deployment on mobile terminals. MobileNet series networks have achieved excellent performance in edge scenarios. In this paper, we propose a low power FPGA-based accelerator using MobileNetV2 as the target network. Finally, the accelerator is implemented on Xilinx MPSOC-XCZU9EG FPGA, and achieves 70.8% Top-1 accuracy under 8-bit quantization, using 74% BRAM, 68% DSP, and 85% LUT. The final power consumption is 5.014W at 150M clock frequency.

articleTitle: Superior Performances of Dynamic On-State Resistance in 1.9kV GaN-on-Sapphire HEMT
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Integrated Circuits, Technologies and Applications (ICTA)
abstract: In this paper, the dynamic drain to source on-state resistance behaviors of a 1.9kV GaN-on-Sapphire HEMT are investigated in details under various conditions. Benefiting from the insulation feature of substrate, the GaN HEMTs fabricated on Sapphire possess ultrahigh breakdown voltage beyond 1.9kV. Meanwhile, the GaN-on-Sapphire device exhibits a lower rate of on-state resistance degradation at both 25°C and 225°C, compared with a GaN-on-Silicon device.

articleTitle: A 28-Gb/s PAM-4 Fully-Integrated Optical Receiver with High-Speed Silicon Photodetector in 28-nm CMOS
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Integrated Circuits, Technologies and Applications (ICTA)
abstract: This paper presents a 28-Gb/s PAM4 fully-integrated optical receiver for short-range optical communication in 28-nm CMOS. This receiver incorporates an on-chip silicon photodetector, a peaking-scalable trans-impedance amplifier (TIA) with the single-to-differential current buffer, a two-stage variable gain amplifier, a continuous-time linear equalizer, and an output buffer. A silicon P-Well/N-Well on-chip photodetector in the standard CMOS process with less junction capacitance is employed to realize a bandwidth of 4.53 GHz. The proposed TIA realizes a 0.9-dB high-frequency pseudo-difference mismatch with low power. Moreover, the peaking-scalable operation of TIA is implemented by an adjustable high-pass filter. This receiver achieves a <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbf{71}-\mathbf{dB}\mathbf{\Omega}$</tex> trans-impedance gain and a 28-Gb/s PAM-4 eye diagram with the energy efficiency of 0.41-pJ/bit under 1.0-V supply.

articleTitle: A 120-dB Dynamic-Range, 24-ps-to-781-ps Resolution Reconfigurable Cyclic TDC Based on a 2× Time Amplifier for LiDAR Applications
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Integrated Circuits, Technologies and Applications (ICTA)
abstract: This paper presents a reconfigurable cyclic time-to-digital converter (TDC) based on a 2× time amplifier (RCTA-TDC) for light detection and ranging (LiDAR) applications. A wide dynamic range (DR) is achieved by the proposed seamless reconfigurable technique, which avoids invalid measurement during mode transition through a synchronous refresh of the cyclic number of the TDC. Fabricated in a 180-nm CMOS process, the proposed TDC demonstrates a DR of 120 dB and offers a configurable resolution ranging from 24 ps to 781 ps. At the highest resolution mode, the differential nonlinearity (DNL) and integral nonlinearity (INL) are 0.5 LSB and 0.7 LSB, respectively. The TDC occupies an area of 0.0264 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> with a power consumption of 2.2 mW from a 1.8-V power supply.

articleTitle: An Accurate Deep Learning-Based Thermal Reconstruction Technique for Microprocessors Using Embedded Sensors
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Integrated Circuits, Technologies and Applications (ICTA)
abstract: This paper proposes a deep learning-based thermal reconstruction technique to accurately recover a microprocessor's full thermal maps with a limited number of sensors. A neural network model derived from U-Net is improved to infer comprehensive thermal profiles using limited sensor readings. An integrated thermal simulation framework combining Gem5, McPAt and HotSpot generates training data, and evaluates the technique on a microprocessor running real applications. Results demonstrate that the proposed technique can accurately reconstruct thermal maps and outperform prior methods.

articleTitle: A Compact 2GHz LNA with Multi-Coupled Inductors for LFEM Application in 65nm CMOS
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Integrated Circuits, Technologies and Applications (ICTA)
abstract: In this paper, a compact low-noise amplifier (LNA) with multi-coupled inductors adopted for well input match and area reduction is proposed. To further reduce the requirement for large matching inductance at a low frequency, a weak-coupling network is introduced to reduce the resonant frequency and the 8-shape inductor is designed for the control of small coupling coefficient. Fabricated in 65nm CMOS technology, the LNA provides a gain of 19.1dB and an NF of 1.0dB with an area of 0.4mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>.

articleTitle: A 28/56 Gb/s NRZ/PAM-4 Dual-Mode Transceiver in 28-nm CMOS
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Integrated Circuits, Technologies and Applications (ICTA)
abstract: A 28/56 Gb/s NRZ/PAM-4 Dual-mode Transceiver (TRx) in a 28-nm CMOS process is presented. The quarter-rate transmitter (TX) incorporates a voltage-mode driver with a 4-tap feed forward equalizer (FFE). The half-rate receiver (RX) employs a continuous-time linear equalizer (CTLE), a 3-stage high-speed slicer and a digital clock and data recovery (CDR). A high-speed track-and-regenerate comparator is proposed to improve the settling time in the RX slicer. Measured results show that the TRx achieves 56 Gb/s maximum data rate with chip-on-board assembly. The TX and RX dissipate 125mW and 181.4mW power from a 0.9V supply, respectively.

articleTitle: An Event-Driven Charge Pump Based OCL-LDO with 410nA IQ and 30ns Recovery Time
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Integrated Circuits, Technologies and Applications (ICTA)
